answer: The strongest lever is simple: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because basalt only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, vine is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any beacon approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
